messages.author: fa770d5dac818ed8
messages.subject: modification indices in measurement invariance
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to replicate the example in these slides http://users.ugent.be/~yrosseel/lavaan/multiplegroup6Dec2012.pdf

A significant chi-square is found when comparing the metric and the strong measurement invariance model which indicates there are some noninvariant intercepts.
Modification indices should show me which item intercepts are noninvariant, as shown on slide 26. However, when I request the modification indices I only get modification indices for loadings and correlations, but I don't get the modification indices for the intercepts. I also tried 
md <- modindices(model3,)
md[md$op=="~ 1",]
but I still don't get them. 

I wonder if there is a mistake in the slides, if the syntax has changed, or if lavaan does not show modification indices for item intercepts.

Thanks!
Margarita

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: modification indices in measurement invariance
parts:
The slide is outdated.

In 0.5-20, modindices() does no longer report modification indices for
equality constrained parameters. Instead, you should you the
lavTestScore() function"

lavTestScore(model3)

Yves.

Dear all, 

I also get similar problem regarding Modificatoin Indices. My syntax looks like this :

setwd("c:\\Users\\R") 
entiredata<-read.csv("Woodcock-Johnson Murray_2007.csv")

require(psych)
require(lavaan)
require(psy)
require(dplyr)

entiredata1<- subset(entiredata, racesample<3 & wj==1 & sample==1)
d1<- select(entiredata1, testage, sex, racesample, sample, wj, c01picvocab, c02spatrels, c03memsen, c04visaudit, c05blend, c07vismatch, c08antsyn, c09analsyn, c10numrev, c11concform, c12analogies)
d1 = d1[complete.cases(d1),]

combined.firstorder.model <-'
Gc =~ c01picvocab + c08antsyn + c12analogies
Gf =~ c08antsyn + c09analsyn + c11concform + c12analogies
Gsm =~ c03memsen + c04visaudit + c05blend + c10numrev
Gs =~ c02spatrels + c07vismatch
'

configural.fit<-cfa(combined.firstorder.model, data=d1, group="racesample")
fitMeasures(configural.fit, c("chisq", "df", "pvalue", "cfi", "rmsea", "srmr", "aic", "bic"))
MI.configural<-modificationIndices(configural.fit, standardized=TRUE, power=FALSE, delta=0.1, alpha=0.05, high.power=0.75)
subset(MI.configural, mi>4)

metric.fit<-cfa(combined.firstorder.model, data=d1, group="racesample", group.equal=c("loadings"))
fitMeasures(metric.fit, c("chisq", "df", "pvalue", "cfi", "rmsea", "srmr", "aic", "bic"))
MI.metric<-modificationIndices(metric.fit, standardized=TRUE, power=FALSE, delta=0.1, alpha=0.05, high.power=0.75)
subset(MI.metric, mi>4)

scalar.fit<-cfa(combined.firstorder.model, data=d1, group="racesample", group.equal=c("loadings", "intercepts"))
fitMeasures(scalar.fit, c("chisq", "df", "pvalue", "cfi", "rmsea", "srmr", "aic", "bic"))
MI.scalar<-modificationIndices(scalar.fit, standardized=TRUE, power=FALSE, delta=0.1, alpha=0.05, high.power=0.75)
subset(MI.scalar, mi>4)

But for the scalar invariance, I don't get the MI for ~1. What correction should be applied to my above syntax ? I have tried lavTestScore() and partialInvariance() but none of these functions give me the MI value for the intercepts of each of the observed variables (i.e., cognitive subtests).

Thanks very much for the help.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: modification indices in measurement invariance
parts:
Have you read the reference cited in the manual page for lavTestScore:

Bentler, P. M., & Chou, C. P. (1993). Some new covariance
structure model improvement statistics. Sage Focus Editions, 154,
235-255.

For lavTestScore(scalar.fit, epc=TRUE), you will get three sections:

1) test: this is the global score test (or multivariate Lagrange
Multiplier test), testing the null hypothesis that all the equality
constraints present in 'scalar.fit' hold

2) uni: these are univariate score tests (aka modification indices, or
univariate Lagrange Multiplier tests) testing the null hypothesis that
the individual equality constraints hold

3) epc: these are the expected parameter changes: how will the
parameters in your model change, *if* you release all the equality
constraints (in the 'epc' column); and how would the parameters look
like ('epv' column) if the constraints are released.

Yves.
